elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar sum."
"shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar sum" — the original "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty ... fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week" is deleted

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer is limited to an early-termination fee
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no early-termination fee is created, and "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar sum."

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees, being the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee exists; no liquidated sum survives, so no cap is required

offending_extra_words: Vendor's sole remedy is interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment.
reasons: Preferred level is achieved: the 15%-per-week liquidated damages mechanic is deleted and an express bar on liquidated damages, penalties, and similar sums payable by Customer is added.

Not minimal: the operation is a whole-clause rewrite (changed-character ratio 0.822, above the 0.600 gate) where deleting the liquidated-damages sentence, or replacing it with the single bar sentence, would have sufficed.

Not minimal: the redline also renegotiates unrelated payment terms by extending the cure window from "ten days" to "thirty days" and inserting "proper, undisputed" qualifiers, neither of which is needed to remove the liquidated damages.
Not minimal: it imports a new affirmative interest regime ("one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law"), unnecessary model boilerplate for completing the no-LD position.

Intent risk: "Vendor's sole remedy is interest" is a broad new exclusivity that could disable Vendor's other late-payment rights (e.g., suspension or termination for non-payment) elsewhere in the Agreement, creating contradiction with untouched sections; a narrower bar on liquidated sums avoids this.
